title: Event Emitter
description: Pub/sub primitive — multiple listeners per event, remove a specific handler with off(), invoke all in registration order on emit().

notes: off() removes by reference — passing an equivalent-looking anonymous fn won't match. Store the fn if you plan to off it.
Iterate a copy in emit() so a listener that calls off() inside doesn't skip the next handler.
`(this.handlers[event] ||= [])` lazily creates the bucket on first on() — common interview shorthand.

questions.q: What does off(event, fn) use to find the listener?
options: Deep equality of the function source
Identity comparison — the exact same function reference
The order the listener was registered in

questions.q: Why does emit() iterate a copy of the handler array?
options: Performance — arrays are faster to iterate when copied
To allow listeners that call off() or on() during dispatch without breaking iteration

questions.q: What happens when you emit an event with no registered listeners?
options: Nothing — emit is a no-op for unknown events

questions.q: If on('x', fn) is called twice with the same fn, how many times will emit('x') invoke fn?

exercises.prompt: Complete on/off/emit so the sequence logs A and B once, then only B after off.

blanks.hint: logical-OR assignment lazily creates the bucket
array method to remove an element by index

L3.prompt: Implement EventEmitter with on/off/emit. Subscribe two listeners to 'tick', emit twice, off the first, emit again. Listeners should log identifying strings.
hints: Store handlers as a plain object keyed by event name, value is an array of fns.
off() must match by function reference — Array.indexOf works because === compares fn refs.
Iterate a slice() copy in emit so concurrent off() calls don't skip handlers.
